title: Assurance
description: Evaluate a specific privacy, integrity, numeric, implementation, or deployment claim.
text: An assurance record identifies the exact plan, component versions, threat model, protected values, visible information, corruption and collusion assumptions, numeric policy, environment, procedure, result, and limitations. Reference tests, formal analysis, cryptographic review, transport hardening, deployment inspection, and leakage tests answer different questions. Missing assurance is not a failed test, but it is not a pass. Evidence for participants that follow the protocol does not establish security against malicious behavior. A publication claim must cite the relevant research evidence and keep its limitations. See reading research and evidence for the conceptual boundary and publications and claims for the review requirements. Python SDK example import pllm document = pllm.assure().todict() findings = {finding["id"]: finding for finding in document["findings"]} assert document["idealuniformcontrol"]["outcome"] == "provedinmodel" assert findings["affinelabelreuse"]["outcome"] == "refutedinscope" API: pllm.assure Report scope is bundled assurance fixtures, not universal privacy proof.

title: Benchmarks
description: Measure PLLM systems with reproducible records and compare only equivalent runs.
text: pllm.benchmark(...) measures supported native compiled regions and returns an immutable EvidenceReport. pllm.deploymentbenchmark(request) validates observations supplied by the caller, but cannot prove where they came from. The CLI also exposes the existing real-role loopback runtime as a non-interactive diagnostic through pllm benchmark run: pllm benchmark run \ --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \ --prompt-file prompt.txt \ --max-output-tokens 24 \ --repetitions 3 \ --output benchmark.json The command chooses an ephemeral loopback port, starts the client, preparation, and inference roles, waits for readiness, runs each request, reads the authoritative archive record, and stops the process group. --format json returns a machine-readable CLI envelope and --dry-run starts no services. Every record identifies whether it covers a compiled region, protocol, deployment, complete model, privacy test, or quality test. Compare runs only when the model, body fingerprint, plan, workload, numeric settings, environment, threads, SIMD settings, warmup, repetitions, and cold or warm mode match. The CLI report and local dashboard help diagnose a loopback deployment, but they do not create a canonical research evidence record. See metrics and research experiments. This SDK example requires a PLLM source checkout because it reads the checked-in schemas/fixtures/compile-request.valid.json compile request. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path import pllm fixture = Path("schemas/fixtures/compile-request.valid.json") plan = pllm.compile(fixture.readtext(encoding="utf-8")) report = pllm.benchmark( plan, weights=bytes([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]), input=b"".join(value.tobytes(4, "little") for value in (7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12)), id="docs-region", privacycohort="masked-linear", numericcohort="wrap32", environment={"fixture": fixture.name}, warmups=1, repetitions=3, ) document = report.todict() assert document["scope"] == "region" assert document["planlockdigest"] == plan.planlockdigest assert len(document["samples"]) == 3 API: pllm.compile, pllm.benchmark This checked EvidenceReport is distinct from the loopback diagnostic JSON.

title: Benchmark and inspect runs
description: Run the headless transport benchmark or open the diagnostic dashboard.
text: Use the headless runner for repeatable local measurements: pllm benchmark run --prompt-file prompt.txt --max-output-tokens 24 --repetitions 3 --output benchmark.json The report contains sanitized diagnostic measurements. It is not a canonical research EvidenceReport, and a loopback run does not establish WAN, multi-host, energy, price, quality, or production non-collusion claims. Use the dashboard when you need a visual transport trace: pllm dev dashboard --tiny --tiny uses random generated weights and validates transport behavior only. Interactive runs without --tiny use the configured real model. See benchmark run, dev dashboard, the benchmark SDK guide, and research evidence records.

title: Command-line interface
description: Inspect PLLM records and run local benchmarks from the terminal.
text: The PLLM command-line interface inspects public metadata, runs bounded local benchmarks, and starts the gateway, inference, and preparation service roles. Service commands do not imply production orchestration or make incomplete compiled plans executable. Install the command uv tool install pllm pllm --help This installs the pllm wheel from PyPI in an isolated tool environment. Use uv tool upgrade pllm to update it. Choose a task - Run private inference through the trusted gateway, then connect an SDK or raw HTTP client. - Operate provider roles as independently configured inference and preparation services. - Benchmark and diagnose with the headless runner or loopback dashboard. - Inspect configuration and research without starting a model. Each guide links to exact parser-generated command help under Command reference. Available commands - pllm config validates and exports public configuration. - pllm components lists built-in component descriptions. - pllm benchmark run runs the real client, preparation, and inference roles on loopback and returns a text-free diagnostic record. - pllm research lists research sources, methods, and recipes or assesses a proposed publication record. - pllm gateway starts the trusted loopback API gateway and can co-locate both provider roles for development. - pllm serve starts one inference or preparation role from explicit deployment configuration. - pllm dev contains development-only tools. Run pllm COMMAND --help for the options accepted by a command. Use --format json when another program will consume the result. Inspect configuration Validate a public configuration or export its canonical form: pllm config show examples/pllm.yaml pllm config export examples/pllm.yaml --output experiment.json See config show and config export. Inspect components List component descriptors or inspect one stable component identity: pllm components list --format json pllm components show pllm/cpu --format json See components list and components show. Explore research records Discover records in machine-readable form, then inspect records by stable ID or registry alias: pllm research sources list --format json pllm research sources show R01 pllm research methods show pllm.method.mpcache-structural-adaptation.v1 pllm research recipes show R01 Discovery references: sources list, methods list, and recipes list. Record references: sources show, methods show, and recipes show. Assess a publication request without running a workflow, or generate coding-agent guidance at repository root: pllm research assess examples/publication-assessment.json --format json pllm research agents --output AGENTS.md See research assess and research agents. Run a benchmark The default model is Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: pllm benchmark run \ --prompt-file prompt.txt \ --max-output-tokens 24 \ --repetitions 3 \ --output benchmark.json The command starts and stops all three roles. Use --tiny only for a random-weight transport smoke test. Reports exclude prompts, generated text, token IDs, activation payloads, masks, seeds, and credentials. They are single-host diagnostics, not canonical research EvidenceReport records. See benchmark run. Open the development dashboard The dashboard is development-only. --tiny uses random weights for a local transport smoke test: pllm dev dashboard --tiny See dev dashboard. Continue - CLI reference lists every current command and option. - Local gateway gives the exact public serving commands and config boundaries. - SDK configuration explains configuration files and content identity. - Research methods explains the records returned by pllm research.

title: Inspect configuration and research
description: Validate public experiment data and inspect built-in component or research records.
text: Inspect or export public experiment configuration: pllm config show examples/pllm.yaml pllm config export examples/pllm.yaml --output experiment.json Inspect built-in components: pllm components list --format json pllm components show pllm/cpu --format json Inspect research records without executing their workflows: pllm research sources list --format json pllm research methods list --format json pllm research recipes list --format json These commands report static or author-supplied records. Presence does not prove runtime coverage, evidence quality, security, or publication readiness. Continue to the generated configuration, component, and research references. For autonomous research work, read research agents and the publication workflow.

title: Run private inference
description: Run the trusted gateway locally or connect it to independently operated PLLM roles.
text: Applications connect to the trusted loopback gateway. They do not send ordinary Responses API or Chat Completions API requests to an inference provider. Local development pllm gateway --local --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --local-files-only --api-key local This command starts the gateway plus co-located inference and preparation roles. It exercises the private protocol, but one machine does not demonstrate operator non-collusion. Configured roles pllm gateway --config client.toml The client configuration identifies independently operated HTTPS role endpoints and credentials. The gateway remains inside the client boundary and exposes /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions on loopback. Use the exact gateway command reference for flags. Then choose a tested consumer integration or use the native client boundary directly.

title: Operate provider roles
description: Start authenticated inference and preparation services without exposing application APIs.
text: Provider operators run separate computation roles: pllm serve inference --config inference.json pllm serve preparation --config preparation.json The inference role consumes one-use prepared rows online. The trusted preparation role computes and pushes masked corrections before a response begins. Neither role is an application-facing Responses API or Chat Completions API endpoint. These commands start processes only. They do not provision hosts, certificates, identities, monitoring, rollback protection, or non-colluding operators. Keep credentials in protected configuration or environment variables rather than command arguments. Read the generated references for serve inference and serve preparation, then apply the deployment boundary and preparation pipeline.

title: Compiler
description: Learn how PLLM turns a model plan and component choices into a checked execution plan.
text: Compilation combines a model plan, component choices, workload limits, and policy. It checks operator support, value formats, conversions, numeric settings, party placement, preparation, native kernels, and assurance requirements. The result is an executable plan with a content digest. Numeric semantics and model quality explains why compiling every operator still does not establish generation fidelity. The coverage report names every missing operator, conversion, party role, numeric bound, assurance record, or compatible component version. Required gaps stop compilation instead of triggering a hidden fallback. All model families use the same semantic model format. Current research profiles cannot execute a complete listed model plan. A model adapter can therefore be available while full private inference remains unsupported. This example requires a PLLM source checkout and must run from its repository root because it reads the checked-in compiler fixture. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import compile request = Path("schemas/fixtures/compile-request.valid.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8") plan = compile(request) assert plan.inputshape == (2, 3) assert plan.outputshape == (2, 2) API: Python objects and signatures Compilation rejects unsupported coverage rather than hiding it behind a fallback. Complete model compilation remains unsupported for current research profiles.

title: Add a category
description: Extend the semantic component graph when an existing category cannot express a real contract.
text: Add a category only when existing operator, representation, protocol, conversion, preparation, kernel, compiler, runtime, deployment, metric, search, or assurance contracts cannot express the new capability without ambiguity. Define ownership, descriptor schema, composition rules, lifecycle, validation, compatibility, evidence, public API, CLI discovery, generated reference, documentation, and migration policy together. Do not name a reusable category after one paper or model. No public Python API defines or registers a new category. See current support before proposing this contract.

title: Component standard
description: Required identity, lifecycle, representation, role, capability, evidence, and limitation fields.
text: 1. Choose a semantic category and stable authority-owned identity. 2. Define versioned parameters, lifecycle phase, input and output representations, host requirements, roles, artifacts, and evidence pointers. 3. Implement in the semantic owner, not a paper-named runtime path. 4. Add static discovery and identity tests without importing provider or native runtime code. 5. Add compatibility and operator-coverage tests. 6. Add runtime, benchmark, quality, assurance, and deployment evidence independently when each exists. The canonical contract is design/component-standard.md. Missing fields remain not recorded; empty evidence is not a pass. Python SDK example from pllm.components import getcomponent descriptor = getcomponent("pllm/cpu") record = descriptor.todict() assert record["component"] == "pllm/cpu" assert {"provider", "version", "category", "capabilities"} <= record.keys() Built-in descriptors expose the public fields contributors must keep discoverable. API: pllm.components.getcomponent

title: Contribute
description: Add a model, component, research method, or evidence record without creating a one-off runtime path.
text: Start with the component standard. Model families use shared operations, research methods transform plans, providers expose generic capabilities, and benchmark or assurance results attach to exact versions. Keep identity, implementation, coverage, evidence, quality, privacy, and deployment status separate. Do not add compiler branches named after a paper or hidden registration that exists only in one runtime. No public Python API performs the contribution workflow. See current support before proposing a new public contract.

title: Native plugin ABI
description: Boundary requirements for future independently distributed native capability providers.
text: The installed native module is currently built with PLLM. A stable third-party native plugin ABI is not published. Any future ABI must version ownership, allocation, byte layout, alignment, panic isolation, threading, cancellation, capability negotiation, artifact identity, host-feature detection, and error translation. Python entry points must remain lightweight and side-effect-free during discovery. No public Python API loads third-party native plugins because no stable plugin ABI is published. See current support for the supported built-in boundary.

title: Publish a provider
description: Expose a component implementation without importing it during core discovery.
text: A provider package publishes signed or digest-addressed descriptor metadata, implementation artifacts, host requirements, supported component versions, representations, roles, and evidence references. Discovery reads static metadata before any trusted code executes. Provider identity does not imply operator identity or trust. Loading requires explicit policy, compatibility validation, and artifact verification. Distribution, component, provider, deployment, and evidence versions remain separate. No public Python API publishes or registers provider packages. See current support for the static built-in discovery boundary.

title: Upstreaming
description: Move validated research work into maintained semantic and runtime components.
text: Upstreaming requires locked sources, a clean-room implementation record where applicable, fidelity tests, model-neutral semantics, component identity, compiler coverage, numeric analysis, matched benchmark evidence, scoped assurance, quality evaluation, limitations, and maintenance ownership. A new publication claim also needs a stable method ID and evidence that isolates the contribution from the baseline. Failed and negative results remain useful research records. No public Python API performs upstreaming or turns component presence into an evidence claim. See research records for the reviewable records that precede upstreaming.

title: Conversions
description: Learn how values move between numeric formats, layouts, and owners.
text: Conversions connect components that use different formats. Examples include a quantized tensor to ring values, arithmetic shares to bits, residues to signed integers, a packed matrix to row-major layout, or server shares to client output. Each conversion records bounds, rounding, network traffic, ownership, visible information, and assurance requirements. The compiler can insert only a declared conversion that satisfies both component interfaces. A matching Python or Rust type cannot silently open a private value or allow a lossy cast. No public Python API currently exposes conversion planning or execution. See current Python support. No built-in conversion component is currently published, and that absence does not authorize an implicit cast.

title: Deployment
description: Learn how to assign PLLM roles to authenticated services without changing privacy assumptions.
text: A deployment assigns each protocol role to a process and operator. It records endpoints, authentication, separate credentials, provider identity, storage, capacity, expiration, observability, shutdown behavior, and trust boundaries. Review privacy and threat models before changing that placement. The client must keep plaintext prompts, masks, private scales, model state, and decoding. Client-to-inference, client-to-preparation, and preparation-to-inference connections use different credentials. Changing the URL of an ordinary model API does not make its unmodified SDK private. A loopback pllm benchmark run checks that the services work together on one machine. It does not show that production operators are independent. Deployment assurance must refer to the exact plan and environment being evaluated. The serving integration guide lists the current gateway and provider-role lifecycle commands. Python SDK example from pllm.deployment import Deployment deployment = Deployment.local(root=".pllm/local") assert deployment.tospec() == {"kind": "local", "root": ".pllm/local"} API: pllm.deployment.Deployment This creates configuration only. Generic remote role deployment is not supported.

title: Kernels
description: Understand PLLM's native integer matrix kernels, memory costs, and CPU requirements.
text: pllm-core implements bounded integer matrices, scalar reference code, runtime AVX2 and NEON selection, codecs, quantization, masking, subtraction, and operating system randomness. It copies validated weights into Rust once and reuses them. Python-to-Rust buffer conversions still create copies. Kernel records list required CPU features, threading, input and output formats, supported operations, memory use, and evidence. Moving arithmetic to Rust does not remove protocol messages, offline preparation, client state, or conversion costs. Python SDK example from pllm import ConfigurationError, Cpu kernel = Cpu(threads=4) assert kernel.tospec() == {"component": "pllm/cpu", "params": {"threads": 4}} try: Cpu(threads=0) except ConfigurationError: pass else: raise AssertionError("Cpu accepted a non-positive thread count") API: Python objects and signatures This checks public kernel configuration and its thread bound; it does not execute a model.

title: Arithmetic and Boolean garbling
description: Compare arithmetic and Boolean garbling without treating one primitive as a complete private runtime.
text: Arithmetic garbling works with modular integer values. Boolean garbling works with bit-level circuits, often using half-gates and free-XOR-compatible labels. Lookup tables and weighted paths are ways to represent a computation; they do not provide identical protocol or security guarantees. Moving values between arithmetic and Boolean forms changes range, bit width, truncation, and communication requirements. A fast primitive does not make a complete transformer executable. Correct reference code is also not a substitute for cryptographic review. Read garbling protocols and conversions for the exact interfaces and current limits.

title: Learn
description: Understand PLLM's private inference runtime, research harness, trust assumptions, and evidence.
text: PLLM is a Rust-first, Python-friendly runtime and research harness for private large language model inference across multiple parties. Its goal is to let a client use remote compute without giving any one compute party the complete request, model state, and output. PLLM combines two systems: - The inference runtime assigns work to the client, preparation service, and inference service while preserving an explicit trust boundary. - The research harness turns papers and hypotheses into independent Rust and Python implementations, then records provenance, plans, tests, benchmarks, limitations, and publication review separately. PLLM is being built for high performance, but performance depends on the exact model, protocol, hardware, network, and workload. Privacy depends on the selected protocol, correct implementation, and stated non-collusion assumptions. Treat the project's economic and safety benefits as goals; use evidence records for measured results and current support for executable coverage. Start here if you need to decide whether a PLLM workflow matches your privacy, performance, or deployment requirements: 1. Privacy and threat models 2. Parties and offline work 3. Masked linear inference 4. Arithmetic and Boolean garbling 5. Numeric semantics and model quality 6. Reading research and evidence These pages explain the concepts. The reference section lists exact APIs and schemas. Current support reports which combinations are available. Integrations shows how the trusted local gateway serves OpenAI-compatible SDKs and coding agents.

title: Chat Completions API
description: Connect text and local function-tool clients through PLLM's Chat Completions API adapter.
text: POST /v1/chat/completions maps OpenAI-compatible chat messages onto the trusted gateway's Responses API path. It supports non-streaming and SSE streaming text, system, developer, user, assistant, and tool roles, and local function tools. The adapter maps assistant tool calls and tool results without sending plaintext schemas, arguments, or results to either provider role. Unsupported request controls and non-text message content fail with an error. API resemblance does not establish compatibility with every OpenAI Chat Completions API feature. Use base URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, API key local, and the model ID loaded by the gateway. The official OpenAI Python SDK's non-streaming and streaming Chat Completions API paths pass repository tests. For applications that can use the Responses API directly, prefer Responses API. For OpenAI-compatible AI SDK consumers, see OpenCode.

title: Codex
description: Configure Codex CLI to use PLLM as a custom Responses API provider.
text: Add this provider to user-level ~/.codex/config.toml: This configuration is verified with Codex CLI 0.154.0. model = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct" modelprovider = "pllm" websearch = "disabled" [modelproviders.pllm] name = "PLLM" baseurl = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1" envkey = "PLLMGATEWAYAPIKEY" wireapi = "responses" Set PLLMGATEWAYAPIKEY to local in the Codex process environment. Provider configuration is machine-local, not a project-scoped override. Start the local gateway before opening Codex. The gateway accepts text and function-tool agent traffic. Codex must use wireapi = "responses". Keep websearch = "disabled": provider-built-in web search is unsupported. This configuration does not claim support for image input, hosted tools, or every Codex capability.

title: Integrations
description: Connect OpenAI-compatible SDKs and coding agents to the trusted local PLLM gateway.
text: PLLM puts a client-controlled gateway between an application and the preparation and inference services. The gateway binds to loopback, holds plaintext application state inside the trusted client boundary, and exposes: - POST /v1/responses - POST /v1/responses/compact - POST /v1/chat/completions - GET /v1/models Preparation and inference roles do not receive plaintext prompts, tool schemas, tool arguments, or tool results. They still observe contract-specific metadata such as public model identity, tensor shapes, timing, traffic volume, and approximate sequence length. Review the trust boundary before moving either role. Choose a path - Local gateway starts all roles for development or connects the gateway to separately operated services. - Responses API describes the Responses API surface and conformance evidence. - Chat Completions API covers clients that use /v1/chat/completions. - OpenAI Python SDK uses the official openai client. - OpenAI Agents SDK uses its Responses API model adapter. - Codex configures a custom Responses API provider. - OpenCode configures an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API provider. All-local mode co-locates preparation and inference. It tests transport and development workflows; it does not establish operator separation or non-collusion.

title: Local gateway
description: Start the trusted loopback gateway locally or connect it to separate PLLM services.
text: The gateway is client-controlled and trusted. It binds to 127.0.0.1:8080 by default and uses the local API key local unless configured otherwise. Run all roles locally pllm gateway --local --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct This downloads or reuses the model, starts preparation and inference children on loopback, and keeps the gateway in the foreground. Stop the gateway to stop its children. This mode validates transport and development behavior only. Because both provider roles run under one operator, it does not establish non-collusion. Connect separate roles Create client.toml for the trusted gateway: [client] baseurl = "https://inference.example" apikey = "inference-secret" model = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct" transport = "websocket" preparationbaseurl = "https://preparation.example" preparationapikey = "preparation-secret" Then start the loopback gateway: pllm gateway --config client.toml Run provider roles in their respective environments: pllm serve inference --config inference.json pllm serve preparation --config preparation.json A minimal inference.json is: { "apikeys": ["inference-secret"], "providerpushapikey": "push-secret", "enginemodels": [ { "engine": "masked-transformer-w4a4", "kind": "huggingface", "path": "/srv/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "modelid": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct" } ] } A minimal preparation.json is: { "apikeys": ["preparation-secret"], "enginemodels": [ { "engine": "masked-transformer-w4a4", "kind": "huggingface", "path": "/srv/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "modelid": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct" } ] } Set PLLMINFERENCEURL and PLLMPUSHAPIKEY for the preparation process. Their values must select the inference service and match its providerpushapikey. Replace example URLs, credentials, and model paths with deployment values. Keep gateway credentials separate from both provider-role credentials. See deployment for remaining production limits.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK
description: Run an OpenAI Agents SDK text agent through PLLM's Responses API gateway.
text: Use the Agents SDK Responses API adapter with an AsyncOpenAI client that targets the local gateway: The executable compatibility suite uses openai-agents 0.22.2. import asyncio from agents import Agent, RunConfig, Runner from agents.models.openairesponses import OpenAIResponsesModel from openai import AsyncOpenAI async def main() - None: async with AsyncOpenAI( baseurl="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", apikey="local", maxretries=0, ) as client: model = OpenAIResponsesModel( model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", openaiclient=client, ) agent = Agent(name="PLLM agent", instructions="Reply briefly.", model=model) result = await Runner.run( agent, "Describe the trusted client boundary.", runconfig=RunConfig(tracingdisabled=True), ) print(result.finaloutput) asyncio.run(main()) This path passes a repository integration test against a real local Responses API gateway. The gateway accepts text and local function-tool traffic. Do not enable hosted tools or assume support for every Agents SDK model feature. Tracing is disabled because this configuration does not use an OpenAI-hosted tracing endpoint.

title: OpenAI Python SDK
description: Point the official OpenAI Python SDK at the trusted PLLM gateway.
text: Start the local gateway, then give the official openai client the gateway base URL and local credential: The executable compatibility suite uses openai 3.8.0. from openai import OpenAI with OpenAI( baseurl="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", apikey="local", maxretries=0, ) as client: response = client.responses.create( model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", input="Explain the client trust boundary in one sentence.", maxoutputtokens=64, ) print(response.outputtext) The installed OpenAI SDK passes repository tests for synchronous and asynchronous Responses API, Responses API streaming, Chat Completions API, and Chat Completions API streaming. Those tests establish the exercised client paths, not complete OpenAI API or model-modality compatibility. Use only a loopback gateway URL. The gateway receives plaintext and belongs inside the trusted client boundary; preparation and inference roles do not receive the plaintext prompt.

title: OpenCode
description: Configure OpenCode to use PLLM through its Chat Completions API gateway.
text: Add opencode.json to the project: This configuration is verified with OpenCode 1.18.31. { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "enabledproviders": ["pllm"], "model": "pllm/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "provider": { "pllm": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "name": "PLLM", "options": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", "apiKey": "local" }, "models": { "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct": { "name": "Qwen 2.5 0.5B Instruct via PLLM" } } } } } @ai-sdk/openai-compatible uses the gateway's Chat Completions API route. enabledproviders prevents fallback to another configured provider. Start the local gateway before opening OpenCode. OpenCode custom-tool declarations map to local function tools through the gateway adapter. Text and function-tool traffic is supported. This integration has not established acceptance of every external tool binary or every OpenCode agent feature; test the exact tools and model before relying on them.

title: Responses API
description: Use PLLM's Responses API surface and understand its tested conformance scope.
text: Send Responses API requests to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/responses with a bearer token for the local gateway. The endpoint supports non-streaming and SSE streaming text responses, stored response retrieval and cancellation, continuation with previousresponseid, and local function-call items. POST /v1/responses/compact performs bounded local history compaction. It keeps recent items and marks elided history; it does not ask a provider to generate a semantic summary. Conformance result The gateway passed all 17 conformance tests from OpenResponses against its 2026-04-24 specification at pinned upstream commit 92c12d96d7b61d6d15e2214daa5e9c6000ab6e1c. The run covered the gateway contract exercised by those tests. It does not prove support for every Responses API field, hosted tool, transport, or model modality. Current model traffic is text plus local function tools. Image and file inputs are not model-understood modalities, and provider-built-in tools are not available. Unsupported fields fail instead of being silently accepted. Use the OpenAI Python SDK or OpenAI Agents SDK for tested Python client paths.

title: Masked linear inference
description: Follow seeded one-time masks through offline correction and online matrix evaluation.
text: For public matrix W, preparation material binds a one-time input mask r, output mask s, and ticket. Preparation computes Wr-s and installs it at inference. Online, the client sends x-r; inference combines it with the correction and returns Wx-s; the client adds s. This changes timing, not algebra. Reusing a row reveals relations between activations, so each ticket is consumed once. The inference role must never receive the seed, and the preparation role must not retain masks or collude with inference. Prefill packs a ticket vector and masked matrix per stage. Decode uses one ticket per stage on a persistent connection. See masked-linear protocol for the component boundary.

title: Numeric semantics and model quality
description: Understand how integer arithmetic affects correctness and model output quality.
text: A model description defines the intended operators. An executable plan must also choose integer representations, quantization scales, ring widths, nonlinear approximations, and decoding rules. Each choice can introduce error or overflow. PLLM selects u16, u24, or u32 rings from the maximum signed output of each prepared stage. This prevents overflow in that stage. It does not show that a complete generation matches the source model. Quantized token lookup and output head behavior also depend on the bundle schema and matrix orientation. Report numeric error, overflow analysis, token agreement, and task quality as separate results. See numerics and representations.

title: Parties and offline work
description: Learn what each party does before and during a private inference request.
text: The client holds plaintext and authorizes each request. The preparation service creates one-time protocol material before a request. The inference service consumes that material while evaluating the model. A provider implements a component. An operator controls a deployed process and its policy. For public-weight inference, preparation commits to the model, transformer body, stages, quantization, and retry limit. It expands seeds supplied by the client into input masks, output masks, and one-time tickets. It computes corrections, sends them to inference, and waits for confirmation. During inference, only the client and inference service exchange tickets and masked activations. Reserved rows can be used only once. Cancellation, failure, replay, or early completion invalidates every unused row in that reservation. See preparation and deployment.

title: Privacy and threat models
description: Learn what PLLM protects, what each party can see, and which trust assumptions still apply.
text: To evaluate a private inference system, ask six questions: 1. Which values should remain private? 2. Which metadata can each party see? 3. Which parties must follow the protocol? 4. Which parties must not collude? 5. Who receives the output? 6. What evidence supports each answer? In PLLM's prepared public-weight path, prompts, decoded output, seeds, masks, private scales, and model state stay with the client. The preparation and inference services both hold the public transformer body. Preparation receives stage seeds before inference starts. Inference receives prepared corrections and masked integer tensors later. This path assumes that both services follow the protocol and do not collude. If you run preparation yourself, that trust stays within your own boundary. Two services controlled by the same operator do not provide meaningful non-collusion. Authentication and replay controls protect the transport, but they do not protect against every malicious participant. Timing, traffic volume, public model identity, tensor shapes, and approximate sequence length may remain visible. Use research evidence records to evaluate a specific privacy claim. Do not infer privacy from the number or names of the services alone.

title: Reading research and evidence
description: Learn how PLLM connects papers, clean-room implementations, measurements, and publication claims.
text: PLLM records each step from a paper to a published result. It keeps the original source, clean-room method, component version, plan history, benchmark evidence, assurance evidence, and proposed claim separate. Citing a paper does not mean it was reproduced. Passing a unit test does not mean a complete model is supported. A benchmark does not prove privacy. Compare results only when the model, model-body fingerprint, plan, numeric policy, workload, environment, cold or warm mode, and metric definitions match. Keep limitations and failed attempts in the record. Missing evidence is not a pass. Continue with method implementation records, research evidence boundaries, and the reproduction workflow.

title: Metrics
description: Choose clear performance, resource, quality, and privacy measurements for a PLLM experiment.
text: No single number describes system performance. Report tokens per second, time to first token, per-token latency, peak and retained memory, CPU time and use, online and offline network traffic, disk use, preparation work, and failures. Energy and price require measurements from the stated environment. Define each metric's scope and denominator. Keep prefill separate from decode, client from provider, offline from online, cold from warm, and useful output from attempted work. Record model quality and privacy assurance separately from performance. Telemetry must never include prompts, generated text, token IDs, activations, seeds, masks, or credentials.

title: Gemma 4
description: Variant-parameterized text-decoder lowering for exact Gemma 4 E2B and E4B configurations.
text: The Gemma 4 adapter validates exact outer text-decoder contracts for: Adapter Repository revision Raw configuration SHA-256 --- --- --- pllm.gemma4e2btext.v1 google/gemma-4-E2B-it@3e22461f65e89153144f8adb70e3b8c2cc9845a7 1b28f3d2c3100f6c594754b81107428bd7b822a7f48272ca681dae9d2ec38330 pllm.gemma4e4btext.v1 google/gemma-4-E4B-it@ee0ef6023621cff504d758262d4e04895a5af4a2 33b10c02df3c2e8536cf323d29d53262aaa2f4d11dbe19bc729373fbe90295d4 Both plans preserve alternating local/global attention, two head widths, Q/K normalization, PLE, shared-KV suffix state, GeLU-tanh branches, branch-output normalization, and final softcap. E2B additionally doubles effective MLP width in its shared suffix. Variant dimensions and layer schedules are data-driven; compiler paths remain model-neutral. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/gemma-4-E2B-it-3e22461f-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert operations["layer.14.gateproj"]["outputshape"][-1] == 6144 assert operations["layer.15.gateproj"]["outputshape"][-1] == 12288 assert operations["layer.34.attentionscores"]["inputs"][1] == "layer.14.keyappend" API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the pinned E2B fixture. Lowering does not execute weights.

title: Models
description: See which model configurations PLLM can describe and what model support does not yet include.
text: pllm.lowermodel(config, batch=..., maxinputtokens=..., maxnewtokens=...) turns model configuration and workload limits into a ModelPlan. It does not download weights or tokenizers, choose a device, or start a runtime. Each adapter validates a specific architecture and produces the same model-neutral plan format. The plan records operators, layers, weight references, persistent state, workload limits, and source identity. When a new model needs a new operation, PLLM extends the shared vocabulary instead of adding model-specific logic to the compiler. Adapter Validated configuration scope Added semantics --- --- --- pllm.qwen2.v1 dense Qwen2 configuration contract grouped-query attention, rotary position, gated SiLU MLP, KV state pllm.qwen3.v1 dense Qwen3; pinned mini-coder-4b fixture explicit head width, Q/K normalization, bias-free attention pllm.qwen35text.v1 pinned Qwen3.5-4B text decoder hybrid full attention and gated-delta recurrence, convolution and recurrent state pllm.phi4mini.v1 pinned Phi-4-mini-instruct decoder fused QKV, fused gate/up, partial LongRoPE pllm.gemma4e2btext.v1 pinned Gemma 4 E2B text decoder hybrid attention, shared KV suffix, double-wide suffix MLP pllm.gemma4e4btext.v1 pinned Gemma 4 E4B text decoder hybrid attention, shared KV suffix, PLE, softcap Describing a model is not the same as loading its checkpoint or running it privately. Compiler support, output quality, benchmarks, and deployment are also separate. Check current support before choosing a model. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert {"rotaryembedding", "silu", "kvcacheappend"} <= operators API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the checked-in fixture. This creates a semantic plan only.

title: Phi-4 mini
description: Fused-projection and LongRoPE semantic lowering for Phi-4-mini-instruct.
text: pllm.phi4mini.v1 recognizes the phi3 remote-code configuration used by microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct revision cfbefacb99257ffa30c83adab238a50856ac3083. The raw configuration SHA-256 is ac65d86061d3d0d704ee2511fd0eb8713ef19eb6eedba17c3080a4165d5b933b. The adapter emits fused QKV and gate/up projections as linear operations followed by explicit slices. LongRoPE records original context, short and long factor vectors, scaling ratio, and partial rotary width. The tied output head references the token embedding matrix. The upstream model name and adapter identity are Phi-4 mini even though the checked configuration discriminator is phi3. This page does not claim checkpoint import or runtime execution. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Phi-4-mini-instruct-cfbefac-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert operations["layer.0.qkvlinear"]["outputshape"] == (1, 16, 5120) assert operations["layer.0.ropeq"]["attributes"]["ropetype"] == "longrope" API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the pinned fixture. Lowering does not import or execute its checkpoint.

title: Qwen2
description: Dense Qwen2 semantic lowering and its present execution boundary.
text: pllm.qwen2.v1 lowers bounded prefill and decode graphs for dense qwen2 configurations. It records grouped-query attention, rotary positions, QKV bias, bias-free output and MLP projections, gated SiLU, KV-cache transitions, last-token output-head evaluation, greedy selection, and feedback. This adapter is structurally validated rather than bound to one repository revision. Checkpoint loading and complete compiler coverage remain separate. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is the current runtime and loopback benchmark target, not evidence that every Qwen2 semantic plan is executable. Python SDK example from pllm import lowermodel config = { "modeltype": "qwen2", "hiddensize": 896, "intermediatesize": 4864, "numhiddenlayers": 1, "numattentionheads": 14, "numkeyvalueheads": 2, "vocabsize": 151936, "maxpositionembeddings": 32768, "hiddenact": "silu", "rmsnormeps": 1e-6, "ropetheta": 1000000.0, "tiewordembeddings": True, } plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert operations["layer.0.klinear"]["outputshape"] == (1, 16, 128) assert operations["layer.0.silu"]["operator"] == "silu" API: Python SDK objects and signatures This self-contained configuration exercises the structural Qwen2 contract without requiring a source-checkout fixture. It creates a semantic plan only.

title: Qwen3 and mini-coder
description: Dense Qwen3 lowering with explicit head width and Q/K normalization.
text: pllm.qwen3.v1 extends dense lowering with explicit headdim, per-head Q/K RMS normalization, and configuration-controlled attention bias. Attention projection width is numattentionheads headdim; it is not assumed equal to hidden width. The checked fixture is ricdomolm/mini-coder-4b revision c87892d046a62415a349a6b3aa244bb630fb7417, raw configuration SHA-256 fdbc9e0615fcb88b2cc37aa2b23fa332b3863068d50092aa6bd1e628fd187c92. This establishes configuration parsing and semantic-plan validation only. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert operations["layer.0.qnorm"]["operator"] == "rmsnorm" assert operations["layer.0.ropeq"]["outputshape"][-1] == 128 API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the pinned mini-coder fixture. This does not execute the model.

title: Qwen3.5
description: Hybrid full-attention and gated-delta semantic lowering for Qwen3.5-4B.
text: pllm.qwen35text.v1 lowers the text decoder in Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B revision 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a. The upstream configuration SHA-256 is ddc63e1c717afa86c865bb5e01313d89d72bb53b97ad4a8a03ba8510c0621670; the checked fixture adds one repository newline and is verified against both representations. The plan retains the exact 3:1 linear/full layer schedule. Linear layers represent fused input projection, causal convolution state, Q/K L2 normalization, gated-delta decay and update, recurrent matrix state, and gated RMS normalization. Full-attention layers represent doubled query projection, Q/K normalization, partial multimodal rotary sections, KV state, and output gating. MTP configuration remains identity-bound but outside the base decoder graph. These newly explicit operators currently report missing compiler coverage. Semantic lowering does not claim an executable Qwen3.5 runtime, checkpoint importer, generation quality, or protected recurrent protocol. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert operations["layer.0.linearattention.gateddeltarule"]["operator"] == "gateddeltarule" assert operations["layer.3.selfattention.qrope"]["attributes"]["mropesection"] == (11, 11, 10) API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the pinned fixture. Inspecting its plan is not an execution claim.

title: Numerics
description: Understand PLLM's integer arithmetic, quantization, rounding, approximation, and overflow checks.
text: A numeric policy records the number domain, scales, rounding, signed decoding, modulus, wire width, coefficient limits, approximation method, and allowed error. Its digest is part of the executable plan and related evidence. Read numeric semantics and model quality for how these choices affect overflow, token agreement, and model behavior. The native matrix core validates dimensions and coefficients, selects a scalar or SIMD kernel at runtime, and uses bounded integer arithmetic. Native execution does not remove quantization error, conversions, protocol messages, or client state. Tests must cover reference arithmetic, boundary values, overflow rejection, and a trusted comparison for each approximation. Token agreement and task quality need separate end-to-end evidence. The first locked nonlinear profile is pllm.numeric.silu.quadraticq7.v1: signed Q7 inputs in [-128, 128], scale 128, deterministic ties-to-even rounding, and a declared encoded-domain SiLU error bound of 0.02285. The compiler includes the numeric type in the protected plan and rejects other numeric representations for this kernel. Python SDK example import numpy as np from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, TrustedPreprocessor mpc = AuthenticatedMPC(TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=0)) decoded = mpc.centered(np.array([0, 32768, 65536], dtype=np.int64)) assert decoded.tolist() == [0, 32768, -1] API: Python objects and signatures This shows center decoding in the reference arithmetic path; it does not establish full-model numeric fidelity.

title: SiLU activation
description: Compile and evaluate PLLM's bounded experimental Q7 SiLU component.
text: PLLM implements one executable SiLU profile: pllm.numeric.silu.quadraticq7.v1. It encodes [-1, 1] at scale 128, evaluates x / 2 + x² / 4, rounds ties to even, and rejects inputs outside the locked domain. Across all 257 encoded inputs, absolute error against SiLU is at most 0.02285. One compiled Q7 SiLU region is capped at 128 elements in this initial bounded slice. The protected implementation uses modulus 257 across the bounded Q7 input and output domains. Client wire encodings and evaluator gates remain separate. Evaluator material is serialized for transport, bound to the compiled plan, consumed once, and burned on an invalid evaluation attempt. This is an experimental reference component, not a complete Qwen execution profile or a production-security claim. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) silu = next( operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"] if operation["operator"] == "silu" ) assert silu["id"] == "layer.0.silu" assert silu["outputshape"] == (1, 16, 9728) API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the model-adapter test fixture. ModelPlan.prefill and its operation records are read-only mappings. The semantic plan preserves SiLU as an explicit operator. A separately validated compile request can lower a bounded SiLU region to the internal native Q7 evaluator, but PLLM does not expose that evaluator through the stable Python runtime facade.

title: Operators
description: Learn how PLLM describes model operations independently of model family and runtime.
text: Operators describe what a model does without depending on model-family names or a specific runtime. Plans represent projections, normalization, rotary embeddings, attention, recurrent and convolutional state, nonlinear activation, residuals, selection, and input or output boundaries with explicit shapes and settings. A compiler profile lists the operators it can execute. Unknown or unsupported operations appear in PlanCoverage and stop compilation. PLLM never silently replaces them with plaintext or approximate work. Research methods also use these shared operators instead of relying on model-specific weight names. An operator in a model plan shows only that PLLM can describe it. Read numeric semantics and model quality for why operator coverage alone is insufficient. See compiler for execution support and numerics for integer and approximation requirements. The bounded SiLU activation is the first operator with an experimental plan-bound protected executor. Other listed operators remain semantic records until their compiler and runtime coverage is implemented. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert {"linear", "rotaryembedding", "silu", "softmax"} <= operators assert plan.coverage().complete is False API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the checked-in fixture. This inspects semantic operators; it does not establish execution coverage.

title: Projection and rotary variants
description: Represent fused projections, tensor slices, head widths, and rotary position rules.
text: A fused checkpoint tensor remains one linear operation followed by semantic slice operations. This preserves storage identity without teaching a compiler model-specific tensor names. Query width, KV width, head count, and head width are independent shape facts. rotaryembedding attributes distinguish ordinary RoPE, partial rotary width, multimodal sections, and LongRoPE short/long factors. A compiler must implement the declared variant or report it missing; it cannot silently substitute ordinary full-width RoPE. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Phi-4-mini-instruct-cfbefac-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} assert operations["layer.0.qslice"]["inputs"] == ("layer.0.qkvlinear",) assert operations["layer.0.ropeq"]["attributes"]["rotarydimensions"] == 96 assert len(operations["layer.0.ropeq"]["attributes"]["longfactor"]) == 48 API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the pinned Phi-4 fixture. This reads plan records only; support still depends on compiler coverage.

title: Stateful recurrence
description: Represent convolution and recurrent state in a hybrid decoder plan.
text: Hybrid decoders declare convolution and recurrent state separately from key/value cache state. causalconvolution consumes prior convolution state while convolutionstateupdate produces the next bounded state. gateddeltarule consumes normalized Q/K, value, decay, beta, and prior recurrent state; gateddeltastateupdate records the corresponding state transition. Separate result and state-transition operations avoid implicit multi-output graph edges. Their shared inputs and attributes bind both records to one semantic update. rmsnormgated, gateddeltadecay, and sigmoid retain the surrounding gating equations. Presence in a validated plan is not implementation coverage. Current compiler profiles fail closed on these operators. Python SDK example from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} missing = [row["operator"] for row in plan.coverage().operators if row["level"] == "missing"] assert {"causalconvolution", "gateddeltarule", "gateddeltastateupdate"} <= operators assert "gateddeltarule" in missing API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the pinned Qwen3.5 fixture. This reports unsupported operators without executing them.

title: Pipeline
description: Combine model, privacy protocol, preparation, runtime, and deployment choices in one configuration.
text: A Pipeline records what you intend to run. Profiles provide visible defaults, and component overrides keep their versions. The configuration digest covers normalized values, not live connections or provider state. Creating a pipeline does not run anything. Model lowering, research transforms, compilation, deployment, preparation, and session creation are separate steps. Each step returns a record or a structured error. The parties and offline work overview explains why preparation and live inference remain distinct. Run pllm config show to inspect examples/pllm.yaml without loading a model or runtime. Python SDK example from pllm import Cpu, MaskedLinear, Model, ModelAwareCorrections, Pipeline pipeline = Pipeline.fromprofile( "baseline.maskedlinearcpu", model=Model("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"), components={"linear": MaskedLinear(), "preparation": ModelAwareCorrections(), "kernels": Cpu()}, ) spec = pipeline.tospec() assert spec["components"]["linear"] == {"component": "pllm/masked-linear", "params": {}} assert spec["components"]["kernels"]["params"]["threads"] == 1 API: Python objects and signatures This creates public configuration only; it does not start a runtime.

title: Preparation
description: Prepare one-time masked material before a private inference request starts.
text: Preparation components define how one-time material is created, batched, committed, transferred, confirmed, erased, expired, and invalidated. They also identify who owns the material and how much can be stored. Protocol and kernel choices remain separate. The parties and offline work overview explains the role boundary. For public masked-linear inference, the client sends seed batches to preparation. Preparation computes corrections, and inference stores them in a sealed inventory. The client refills inventory only while idle. A restart or idle timeout discards inventory held in memory. Prepared material is part of the system cost. Benchmarks must state whether preparation and loading are included in cold and warm measurements so the resulting research evidence keeps that scope visible. Python SDK example import numpy as np from pllm import TrustedPreprocessor preparation = TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=7) mask = preparation.inputmask((3,)) reconstructed = (mask.sharedmask.client.value + mask.sharedmask.server.value) % 65537 assert np.arrayequal(reconstructed, mask.clearmaskforclient) API: Python objects and signatures This creates and checks reference one-time material in process. Production use requires a reviewed correlation protocol and separate roles.

title: Arithmetic garbling
description: Mixed-modulus labels and projection gates over bounded arithmetic values.
text: Arithmetic garbling represents values with labels per modulus. Free compatible arithmetic can avoid tables; nonlinear projection reconstructs signed values jointly from a coprime residue bundle and emits output labels. Gate material is shape-bound, strictly serialized, and consumed once. Reference exhaustive correctness, tamper rejection, plan commitments, and one-use process-local burn checks establish implementation behavior only. The compiler can select the exact experimental Q7 SiLU projection profile. Cryptographic review, durable replay protection, complete-model coverage, and deployment assurance are not recorded. No public Python API currently exposes the arithmetic-garbling evaluator. See research evidence. The evaluator remains internal to the native compiled-plan boundary and is not part of the stable Python runtime facade.

title: Half-gates
description: Boolean AND-gate representation and the obligations surrounding free-XOR circuit execution.
text: Half-gates reduce encrypted table material for Boolean AND gates under compatible label and hash assumptions. A component contract must bind circuit identity, wire labels, correlation assumptions, evaluator material, one-time use, serialization, and output decoding. PLLM documents this category for composition and research mapping. Presence in the taxonomy does not state that a reviewed native implementation or executable profile exists. No public Python API currently exposes a half-gate component. See research evidence for the evidence boundary; taxonomy alone does not provide executable SDK support.

title: Garbling
description: Reference arithmetic and Boolean garbling components with explicit maturity and composition boundaries.
text: Garbling is a family of representations and protocols, not one interchangeable backend. PLLM records arithmetic projection gates, Boolean half-gates, lookup tables, and weighted paths separately because their domains, costs, proofs, and conversion obligations differ. Current clean-room arithmetic work is reference-only and unreviewed. It is excluded from executable compiler profiles until protocol, transport, coverage, and assurance gates pass. See research reproductions. No public Python API currently exposes garbling configuration or execution. Follow research reproductions for experimental evidence; the unsupported SDK state is not an execution fallback.

title: Lookup tables
description: Bounded function tables with explicit domains, indexing, leakage, and material size.
text: A lookup-table component maps a finite encoded domain to an encoded range. Its contract records signed interpretation, table cardinality, invalid indices, material ownership, one-time use, communication, and whether selection is data-oblivious under the stated threat model. Tables are useful for nonlinearities only when domain bounds and total storage remain explicit. Approximation and model-quality evidence belong to the numeric policy, not the table name. No public Python API currently exposes a garbled lookup-table component. See research evidence for the evidence boundary; no lookup-table component is currently published through the SDK.

title: Weighted path
description: Decision-path representations for bounded piecewise or tree-structured secure evaluation.
text: Weighted paths encode a sequence of predicates and selected contributions rather than a dense table. A component must state path topology, hidden and public structure, comparison semantics, branching leakage, numeric bounds, and worst-case work. This is an extension category, not a shipped support claim. Candidate research enters through source and method records before any compiler profile can select it. No public Python API currently exposes a weighted-path component. Follow research methods before treating this extension category as an executable support claim.

title: Protocols
description: See how PLLM defines parties, messages, privacy assumptions, and failure behavior.
text: A protocol defines its parties, offline and online phases, inputs, outputs, messages, authentication, replay behavior, one-time material, visible information, trust assumptions, and failure behavior. Model adapters and deployment policy are separate concerns. Start with privacy and threat models before using these implementation interfaces to select a protocol. Current protocols include masked-linear inference and experimental garbling components. Check execution support, security review, assurance, and deployment status separately; apply the research evidence rules to any supporting records. Python SDK example import numpy as np from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, AuthenticationError, TrustedPreprocessor mpc = AuthenticatedMPC(TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=2)) value = mpc.publicvalue(np.array([5], dtype=np.int64)) try: mpc.open(value.tamperclient(valuedelta=1)) except AuthenticationError: tamperdetected = True else: tamperdetected = False assert tamperdetected API: Python objects and signatures This checks authenticated-opening failure behavior in the single-process reference protocol; it does not start separate protocol parties.

title: Masked linear
description: Prepared public-weight linear inference with seeded one-time masks and committed inventory.
text: The prepared protocol separates client, trusted preparation, and untrusted inference roles. Offline, preparation computes Wr-s from domain-separated client seed batches and pushes committed corrections. Online, inference atomically consumes the ticket matching x-r and returns Wx-s for client reconstruction. Inventory identity binds model, body, stage, weight, shape, quantization, ring, modulus, wire width, and attempt budget. Rows are one-use and burned on reservation failure, cancellation, replay, or early completion. Preparation is idle during online chat. This contract assumes protocol-following non-colluding roles and public body weights. Confidential-weight and shared-state protocols are separate. Python SDK example import numpy as np from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, TrustedPreprocessor preparation = TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=3) runtime = AuthenticatedMPC(preparation) x = np.array([[3, -2]], dtype=np.int64) weight = np.array([[2, 1]], dtype=np.int64) maskedx = runtime.input(x, preparation.inputmask(x.shape)) correlation = preparation.linearcorrelation(weight, x.shape) result = runtime.centered(runtime.open(runtime.linear(maskedx, weight, correlation))) assert result.tolist() == [[4]] assert runtime.stats.linearrounds == 1 API: Python objects and signatures This exercises prepared masked linear arithmetic in the single-process reference protocol; it does not provide role separation or deployment assurance.

title: Research workflows
description: Build, reproduce, compare, and review private-inference research with explicit stop rules.
text: A recipe records exact sources, method and component versions, model and workload limits, environment requirements, steps, expected files, evidence, and failure policy. Listing a recipe never runs it. Recipes support reproducibility without making third-party repositories runtime dependencies. PLLM implements methods independently in Python and Rust. Original artifacts remain sources and comparison material only. Run pllm research recipes list to inspect current records. Recipe execution is not supported because sandboxing, artifact identity, and result records are not yet available together. Use the pages in this section to choose a workflow. Build and reproduction work must stop rather than silently substituting an upstream runtime, weakening the privacy boundary, or presenting unmatched measurements as comparable evidence.

title: Native reference
description: Rust crates, the Python binding, data ownership, threading, and ABI support.
text: pllm-core owns validated integer matrices and native execution. pllm-models owns model-neutral semantic lowering. Research-method crates transform semantic plans. pllm-types owns canonical records; pllm-compiler validates executable plans. pllm-python contains only the PyO3 boundary exposed as pllm.native. The Python binding copies bytes into validated integer buffers, releases the interpreter lock around core work, and returns immutable bytes. Matrices own their validated weights; dimensions and contents cannot mutate through public Rust APIs. An executor owns its persistent Rayon pool. The stable Python ABI starts at 3.11. No third-party native plugin ABI is currently published. Python SDK example from pllm.kernels import Cpu descriptor = Cpu.describe() assert descriptor.distribution == "pllm" assert "cpu" in descriptor.capabilities This inspects built-in metadata without loading a third-party plugin. API: pllm.kernels.Cpu

title: Python reference
description: The installed pllm namespace and its generated public API inventory.
text: python/pllm is the only installed namespace. Public objects are imported on demand so metadata discovery does not load model weights, devices, providers, or runtime state. See the generated pllm package inventory for exact modules, symbols, signatures, and native runtime identities. Python SDK example import pllm from pllm.config import Experiment assert pllm.Experiment is Experiment API: pllm.Experiment

title: Representations
description: Understand how PLLM records a value's format, owner, bounds, and encoding.
text: A representation states a value's number domain, shape, memory layout, owner, bounds, encoding, and wire format. PLLM uses representations for quantized tensors, ring elements, additive shares, masked activations, CRT residues, garbled labels, packed prefill matrices, and one-time tickets. Each component lists the representations it accepts and produces. Two components can connect only through a compatible edge or an explicit conversion. Matching tensor shapes are not enough. Wire format versions and ownership changes are part of the plan history. No public Python API currently exposes representation compatibility records. See current Python support. Current built-in descriptors do not record representation fields; absence is not compatibility evidence.

title: Experiments
description: Design reproducible experiments with fixed plans, comparable runs, and recorded failures.
text: Before execution, an experiment records its hypothesis, baseline, changed component, model and workload limits, plan digests, environment, metrics, quality requirements, assurance work, stopping rule, and expected artifacts. Report throughput, latency, memory, CPU, online and offline network traffic, disk, preparation work, quality, and assurance separately. Keep failed and negative results. A publication claim must isolate the contribution from its baseline and identify the method unambiguously. See benchmarks, metrics, and publication assessment.

title: Reimplemented papers
description: Trace published private-inference methods to their independent PLLM components, evidence, and current limitations.
text: This catalog is about published work reimplemented as PLLM components. A source record alone does not qualify. Each entry must link the original paper, PLLM's method record, the component that implements it, and the evidence that establishes its current maturity. MPCache MPCache: MPC-Friendly KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Private Large Language Model Inference inspired PLLM's independent pllm.method.mpcache-structural-adaptation.v1 method. It is exposed as the pllm/kv-cache-eviction component and the KvCacheEviction plan transform. - Source and method records - Component catalog - SDK component usage - Current support status The current component transforms compatible Qwen2 semantic plans. It does not reproduce MPCache's complete three-party protected execution, and its fidelity, benchmark, assurance, and protected-execution statuses remain unchecked. Reading copies and PLLM publications Each source record stores authors, title, primary URL, revision, publication details, license, artifact digests, local paper digest, and acquisition status. Local PDFs under papers/ are private reading copies and are not included in the package or website. PLLM's current paper and whitepaper are separate project publications. A citation gives attribution. It does not prove that PLLM reproduced the method, matched a benchmark, or assessed its security.

title: Evidence and records
description: Keep sources, methods, implementations, plans, evidence, assurance, and claims independently reviewable.
text: PLLM research uses immutable, linked records rather than one undifferentiated success status. A paper can be acquired without being reproduced. A component can be implemented without benchmark parity, protected execution, or assurance. A measurement can be valid without supporting a broad publication claim. Use this section to inspect the record types, evidence rules, comparison metrics, and generated catalog. Every public claim should resolve to the exact source, implementation, plan, workload, environment, result, and limitation that support it.

title: Reproductions
description: Reimplement published methods independently in PLLM's Python and Rust stack.
text: PLLM reproductions begin with public papers and locked source records. Contributors then implement the method independently in PLLM. Upstream repositories can help with attribution and comparison, but PLLM does not build them into the runtime or use them as dependencies. The record reports each step separately: source acquired, reference behavior implemented, primitive fidelity tested, native path implemented, model coverage completed, runtime execution available, benchmark matched, privacy assessed, and limitations reviewed. One summary label must not hide a missing step. Follow the clean-room workflow and agent checklist.

title: Runtime
description: Understand which live state a PLLM runtime owns and how it differs from a reproducible plan.
text: A runtime session owns changing state such as inventory reservations, connections, scheduling, the KV cache, native executors, and cancellation. This state is not part of an immutable configuration or plan digest. The Python binding validates input buffers, releases the Python interpreter lock while Rust runs, and returns immutable bytes. Python coordinates models and protocols. Runtime graph support and checkpoint loading remain separate from model planning. Before execution, the runtime rechecks plan identity, component support, weights, and required assurance records. The CLI provides explicit gateway, inference, and preparation lifecycle commands; it does not provide generic plan-locked orchestration. See local gateway. Python SDK example import numpy as np from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, TrustedPreprocessor runtime = AuthenticatedMPC(TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=4)) opened = runtime.open(runtime.publicvalue(np.array([7, 8], dtype=np.int64))) assert opened.tolist() == [7, 8] assert runtime.stats.openingrounds == 1 API: Python objects and signatures The opening updates live runtime counters. This in-process arithmetic simulator is not a deployed multi-party session.

title: Python SDK
description: Plan models, compose research methods, and use supported PLLM runtimes from Python.
text: PLLM ships one Python package backed by Rust. The public API separates model planning from live runtime state so you can inspect and reproduce a plan without including credentials, masks, sessions, or model weights. Install the package Add the pllm package from PyPI to a uv project: uv add pllm Python SDK example pllm.lowermodel accepts model configuration and workload bounds. It returns an immutable semantic ModelPlan; it does not load a checkpoint or start an inference session. from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json") plan = lowermodel(fixture.readbytes(), batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) assert plan.todict()["adapter"] == "pllm.qwen3.v1" assert plan.prefill["output"] == "tokenfeedback" API: Python SDK objects and signatures Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include the model-adapter test fixture. Compose research methods Apply a compatible component to a model plan to create a new plan with a record of the transformation. Compatibility with a semantic plan does not by itself establish compiler, runtime, privacy, quality, or deployment support. Run supported workflows Runtime APIs cover specific public-weight and confidential-weight workflows. Support depends on the model, protocol, operator set, deployment, and threat model. Check current support before choosing a path. Continue - Python API reference lists the installed public objects. - Get started covers installation and the first inspection workflow. - OpenAI Python SDK connects the official client to the trusted local gateway. - Runtime explains live state and execution boundaries. - Models separates semantic planning from executable support.

title: Search
description: Compare compatible system designs against explicit resource, quality, and assurance limits.
text: Search uses component records and evidence instead of importing provider code. Each candidate combines model coverage, operator support, value formats, conversions, protocols, preparation, kernels, party placement, and numeric policy. You can limit memory, CPU, network traffic, disk use, latency, throughput, quality loss, trust assumptions, and evidence maturity. Tradeoffs remain visible; PLLM does not declare one plan best for every deployment. Finding a candidate is not proof that it works. A selected plan must compile, run in its stated environment, and produce matching benchmark and assurance records. No public Python API currently executes plan search or applies resource constraints to candidate designs. See current Python support. Static component discovery is not a search result.

title: Run the local development benchmark
description: Run the real PLLM roles on one machine and understand what the result does and does not measure.
text: Run the real local client, preparation, and inference roles: pllm benchmark run \ --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \ --prompt "Explain why private inference matters." \ --max-output-tokens 8 \ --output benchmark.json Review the exact benchmark run options before changing the model, workload, repetitions, or output behavior. The command is headless by default, reports startup and execution progress on the terminal, writes a sanitized JSON report, and stops all three roles. Add --show-dashboard only when you want the interactive local view. Use --tiny only to test transport with generated weights. The report is not a canonical benchmark evidence record. A local run does not measure a multi-host or wide-area deployment, model quality, energy use, price, adversarial behavior, or production non-collusion. Continue with research evidence requirements and metrics before comparing results.
